test.name: Spec 0037 full verify: import, approval, revocation, and repeated requests on a real stacklyd, with a real full disk

expected: on a real stacklyd and stackly CLI in a temporary root, a local package that is not approved can be previewed and inspected but nothing installs, creates, or starts from it; another revision waits for approval again; revoke, remove, and a catalog revocation keep runtimes, instances, and data and existing instances still start; an import that fails on a full disk leaves no store folder of its own and keeps one that was there; eight imports at once leave one row at revision 1; a repeated request runs no second operation
actual: Every check passed. Pending: preview wrote nothing and reported quarantined true with the agent Safari; the import answered trust local, approval pending; the store copy was 0700 and 0600 with no quarantine attribute and the origin folder kept its bytes, modes, and attributes; resolve, install, form, and create answered provider.approval_required, with no operation, instance, runtime, or child process; the two environment variables changed nothing. Approval: the CLI printed the fixture statement word for word; create wrote the pin row with publisher acme and approval approved; revision 0.2.0 became pending with changes revision, download_hosts, endpoints, also in its audit row, and the gate closed again; the first bytes came back approved. Eight imports: eight replies, one row at revision 1, one store folder, eight succeeded operations each with its audit row and one catalog.changed. Repeats: approve repeated after a revoke answered approval revoked with no second operation, audit row, or event; a moved origin folder did not matter; another params answered operation.idempotency_key_reused; after the remove the repeats answered provider.import_not_found reason not_imported and remove answered the same RemovedProvider. Revoke and remove: rows and data, runtime, and pinned folders were the same; every gate, also the pinned revision and duplicate, answered provider.revoked by user; the existing instance started, restarted, and stopped. The pin with no approval answered provider.approval_required for form, create, and duplicate. Catalog revocation: approve and every gate answered provider.revoked by catalog with catalog revision 12 and since 2026-11-01; the list named the catalog revision and its publish date; no CLI text said latest or up to date. Full disk: both imports answered provider.store_failed reason no_space; no folder of acme/bigc was left (its store item ended compensated), the folder that was there stayed with its changed bytes (item not_owned), no row changed, and no catalog.changed was published; the repeats answered the same error with no new operation; new keys repaired the first package with its approval kept and imported the second. Home: originPath was ~/pk/fakeish everywhere, and no audit row or log line held the home path; the CLI results were the same DTOs; after a restart the entry and its decision were the same; a deleted store folder gave an invalid local entry that the same bytes repaired with the approval kept. One low note: the audit row of an import that fails in its read or store step holds no provider or digest, because the note is set in the commit step.
steps: on commit 242b795b with a clean tree: `cargo build -p stacklyd -p stackly-cli -p stackly-fake-server` and `cargo build -p stacklyd --example skeleton_seed`; every probe ran a real stacklyd and the stackly CLI in its own temporary STACKLY_ROOT seeded by skeleton_seed (fake runtime 0.1.0), with a development catalog of revision 11 in STACKLY_CATALOG_DIR; requests went over the socket from a small length prefixed JSON client and from the CLI; the registry was read with sqlite3 in read only mode

pending: preview and import of a copy of the fake package with the ID acme/fakeish whose provider.yaml carried a com.apple.quarantine attribute written with xattr; then runtime.resolve, runtime.install, instance.get_create_form with and without the provider, and stackly instance create; the daemon ran with STACKLY_TRUST=1 and STACKLY_APPROVE_ALL=1 in its environment

approval: stackly provider approve on a pty answered y, the printed statement compared with protocols/fixtures/provider/approval-statement.txt; stackly instance create from the approved entry, start, restart, stop; import of revision 0.2.0 with another download host and port; import of the first bytes again
eight provider.import requests of the same bytes sent at once on eight connections with eight keys, with an events.subscribe connection open

repeated requests: import, approve, and revoke repeated with their first keys after a revoke, after the origin folder moved, and after a remove; remove repeated with its key; a key reused with other params; an approve that was answered without an operation repeated after a revoke

revoke and remove through the CLI with and without --yes, with the runtime, instance, and artifact rows and the data folders compared before and after; every gate again, also create and duplicate from the pinned revision; start, restart, and stop of the existing instance after each

with the daemon stopped, provider_revisions.approval of the pinned acme/fakeish row set to NULL in the temporary registry, to stand for a pin made before the gate existed; then form, create, and duplicate from that pin
restart with a catalog of revision 12 whose revoked list names acme/fakeish 0.1.0; preview, import, approve, every gate, the existing instance, stackly provider list and inspect

full disk: a 96 MB APFS disk image mounted in the session scratchpad held the whole STACKLY_ROOT; a package with a 1 MB versions.json was imported and approved, one byte of its stored copy was changed, the volume was filled, then a second package (acme/bigc) and the first package again were imported; after the volume was freed both requests were repeated with their first keys and then with new keys; the image was detached and deleted

a daemon with HOME set to a temporary folder that held the package: originPath in the preview, the unreadable folder error, the detail, the audit rows, and the daemon log; import --json, import --approve with and without --yes, approve, revoke, remove with --json; a restart; a restart after the store folder was deleted, then an import of the same bytes
reviewer: Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2) as the checker of the full verify session chk-f37-verify ran the probes and read their output, the temporary registries, and the daemon logs; the user has not reviewed this record
